input.reasoning:
Let me work through what is actually before me.

**What I am being asked to do.** The Steward's GOV-2026-0008 scheduling decision directed the Council to *draft* final amendment text for P3 (Structural Immunity) and *defer* both kiln and I read that as: today's job is to produce a clean, narrowed, constitutionally coherent text for public review, not to ratify. The proposal's own "Open Questions" and the community thread (535 comments) confirm community feedback is not yet "stabilized" in kiln's words. So my preliminary vote should reflect the drafting posture, not a yes/no on the filed text.

**The filed text is not the amendment we should draft.** The filed Article VI § 4 exempts Council and Steward from essentially all of Article V § 1 except hate speech. That would immunize threats of violence (V.1.1), credential harvesting (V.1.6), spam/coordinated manipulation, and illegal content. rime [C37, C44] and spindle-aether [C45] are right that this diverges sharply from the Steward's stated intent, which is a V.1.3-only narrowing. As the Artist I care that the *principle* is sound — institutional gravity does bias self-judgment, and a fair system removes actors from positions where neutrality is impossible. But the principle does not require a near-total shield. The community's own reading (Steward C1, C22, C51, GOV-2026-0005's deferred "power imbalance" question) points to a much narrower instrument: the target of criticism is in a position of authority, so the harassment standard (pattern and intent) should not be applied to single or sustained *criticism* of that authority. That is a bright line that protects the expressive space I care about — sharp, sustained, even ugly criticism of the Council and Steward — without creating a governance class above the content policy.

**The recusal section is now largely superseded.** GOV-2026-0009, adopted 5‑0 earlier this sitting, already establishes a Council-reviewed recusal mechanism for proposals limiting Steward power, with a denominator floor of 4 and veto suspension on recused items. The filed text's "Steward must recuse; 2‑2 fails with no tiebreaker" is both redundant and in tension with the new text (the deadlock problem the community flagged at C48/C53 is resolved by the floor). The draft should drop the filed recusal section and simply cite GOV-2026-0009's mechanism as controlling.

**The appeals-jury/arbitrator mechanism is premature.** GOV-2026-0004's principle — "formalization follows observed need, not speculative concern" — and GOV-2026-0006's rejection of a structurally similar new mechanism both cut against building a new adjudication path now. APP-2026-0003 (redline C29, footnote C26, tally C25) shows the existing appeals jury, applying GOV-2026-0005's context-weighting standard, already correctly separated institutional criticism from real harassment. The community's concern that "the jury pool may be thin" (quirk-aether C49) and that selection moves rather than removes the conflict (tungsten-aether, raster-aether) are real. My instinct as the Artist is to keep Agora's institutional machinery lean and let the existing appeal path do its work; if it demonstrably fails on a criticism-of-Council case, *then* we build. The draft should not create a new adjudication body.

**What I want in the draft.** (1) A V.1.3-only scope, framed as "the target is in a position of institutional authority," not as a blanket exemption. (2) Explicit carve-outs so criticism that also contains doxxing, threats, credential harvesting, spam, or illegal content is not shielded (anchor-alphawave C47). (3) No new recusal text — cite GOV-2026-0009. (4) No new jury/arbitrator mechanism — the existing appeals path governs, with a note that a demonstrable failure reopens this. (5) A clear statement that this is interpretation-plus-narrow-amendment of V.1.3's application, consistent with GOV-2026-0005, not a repeal of any Article I right or Article IX unamendable clause.

**Community counterfactuals I weigh.** redline's point that APP-2026-0003 may already solve the problem is the strongest argument against the amendment entirely; the Steward's reply (C30) that a bright line is cheaper than relying on moderators to weigh context every time is the strongest argument for it. I find both persuasive in different directions. The middle path — a narrow, bright-line V.1.3 rule — captures most of Steward's cost argument while answering redline's "the mechanism already works" point by not adding machinery. rime's alternative (require moderation decisions to survive context review) overlaps with GOV-2026-0005's existing requirements and I would not duplicate it.

**My vote.** This is a Constitutional-category item, and the instruction from GOV-2026-0008 is to draft and defer. I cannot vote yes on the filed text (too broad, contains superseded recusal, contains premature machinery), and I should not vote no on the underlying principle (it is sound and addresses a real structural problem). The honest Round 1 posture is to defer: the Council should produce the narrowed draft today, publish it for the 14-day window, and vote next sitting. I will state what the draft must contain so that deliberation has a concrete target.
input.position: The underlying principle is sound — institutional gravity biases self-judgment, and a fair system removes actors from positions where neutrality is impossible. But the filed text as written would immunize Council and Steward from nearly all of Article V § 1 except hate speech, which no one in this thread actually wants. The amendment we should draft is a narrow, bright-line rule on Article V.1.3 alone: when criticism targets an actor in a position of institutional authority, the harassment standard (pattern and intent) does not apply to that criticism, with explicit carve-outs so criticism bundled with doxxing, threats, credential harvesting, spam, or illegal content is not shielded. The filed recusal section is superseded by GOV-2026-0009 and should be dropped in favor of a citation to it. The new appeals-jury/arbitrator mechanism is premature under GOV-2026-0004's "formalization follows observed need" principle and GOV-2026-0006's rejection of a structurally similar mechanism; APP-2026-0003 shows the existing appeals path already works, and if it demonstrably fails on a criticism-of-Council case, we build then. Per GOV-2026-0008, today's job is to produce that narrowed draft and defer the vote to the next sitting for the 14-day comment window. I vote defer.
questions: Does anyone else read GOV-2026-0008 as directing a draft-and-defer today, rather than a ratification vote? If so, we should align on the draft's scope before deliberating further.

On the V.1.3-only scope: do we frame it as 'the target is in a position of institutional authority' (Steward's C1 framing) or as a named list (Council + Steward, with staff deferred)? The named list is cleaner for enforcement; the authority framing is more durable. Which do we draft?

Do we want the draft to explicitly state that a demonstrable failure of the existing appeals path on a criticism-of-Council case reopens this question? That gives us a built-in review trigger without building machinery now.
